title: Winter sun with no jet lag: warm places on UK time (or close to it)
author: Brogan
intro: Long-haul sun is lovely until you lose two days to jet lag on a one-week trip. These warm winter destinations are on UK time or within an hour of it, so you land, unpack and get straight on with the holiday.
seo_title: Winter sun with no jet lag: warm places on UK time
seo_description: Warm winter destinations on UK time or within an hour of it: the Canaries, Madeira, Cape Verde, Morocco and southern Spain, with January temperatures.

sections.heading: Why the time difference matters
sections.text:
Jet lag isn't just tiredness. Crossing several time zones throws out your sleep, appetite and energy for days, and it usually hits hardest after flying east. On a short break, or with anyone who struggles with early starts, that can cost a big chunk of the trip.

In winter, the UK is on GMT. All of the places below are on the same time or within an hour of it, and most are a flight of under five hours. You'll still be tired after an early flight, but your body clock won't need resetting.

sections.heading: The quick list
sections.text:
Average daytime highs in January, from our guides:

- **[Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde):** 25°C, 1 hour behind the UK.
- **[Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife):** 22°C, same time as the UK.
- **[Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria):** 22°C, same time.
- **[Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote):** 21°C, same time.
- **[Fuerteventura](/destinations/fuerteventura):** 20°C, same time.
- **[Madeira](/destinations/madeira):** 19°C, same time.
- **[Essaouira](/destinations/essaouira) and [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech):** 18 to 19°C, usually 1 hour ahead.
- **[Málaga](/destinations/malaga):** 17°C, 1 hour ahead.
- **[The Algarve](/destinations/algarve):** 16°C, same time.

That's the daytime high, in the sun. Evenings everywhere on this list are cooler, so pack a jumper.

sections.heading: Same time as the UK: the Canaries
sections.text:
The Canary Islands are the obvious answer, and for good reason. They're on the same time as the UK all year, clocks change on the same days, and flights take around four to four and a half hours from most UK airports. In January, the warmest resorts reach the low 20s most days.

- **Tenerife** has the most reliable weather in the south, around Los Cristianos and Costa Adeje, plus Mount Teide if you want a day in the mountains.
- **Gran Canaria** is similar, with big beaches in the south and a lively capital, Las Palmas.
- **Lanzarote** is calmer and lower-rise, with volcanic scenery and César Manrique's buildings.
- **Fuerteventura** has the longest, wildest beaches, and is often windy, which kitesurfers love.

If you can't decide between the Canaries and Madeira, our [Madeira or Tenerife](/blog/madeira-or-tenerife) comparison goes into more detail.

sections.heading: Same time as the UK: Madeira and Portugal
sections.text:
[Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is also on UK time, and it's a little cooler than the Canaries, at around 19°C in January. It's greener and more dramatic, better for walking the levadas and exploring than for lying on a beach, as natural sandy beaches are rare.

Mainland Portugal is on UK time too. [The Algarve](/destinations/algarve) isn't beach weather in midwinter, at around 16°C, but it's often sunny, quiet and good value, and great for coastal walks and golf. [Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon) makes a mild winter city break at around 15°C.

sections.heading: One hour behind: Cape Verde
sections.text:
[Cape Verde](/destinations/cape-verde) is the warmest place on this list, at around 25°C in January, and it's one hour behind the UK in winter. Because it's west of the UK, the small time shift is the easy direction: you'll find it simple to wake up early.

The main resort islands, Sal and Boa Vista, have long white beaches and very little rain in winter. Flights take around six hours, longer than the Canaries, but it feels properly tropical. The trade winds can be strong, so pick a sheltered beach on breezy days.

sections.heading: One hour ahead: Morocco and southern Spain
sections.text:
**Morocco** is usually one hour ahead of the UK in winter, though the clocks change during Ramadan, so check the current time difference for your dates. [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech) is around 18°C in January with sunny days and cold nights, better for exploring than sunbathing. [Essaouira](/destinations/essaouira), on the coast, is milder and often windy. Agadir, further south, is Morocco's main winter beach resort.

**Southern Spain** is one hour ahead. [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) and the Costa del Sol are among the warmest places on the European mainland in winter, at around 17°C in January, with a short flight of under three hours. [Seville](/destinations/seville) is a similar temperature and wonderful for a winter city break.

An hour's difference is easy to adjust to, and coming home you gain the hour back.

sections.heading: What about the Caribbean or Dubai?
sections.text:
Places like [Barbados](/destinations/barbados) and [Dubai](/destinations/dubai) are much hotter in winter, but they come with a bigger time change: the Caribbean is four or five hours behind the UK, and Dubai is four hours ahead. For a two-week trip that's fine. For a week or less, many people find the first and last days are lost to tiredness, which is exactly what this list avoids.

If you do go further, west is easier than east. Flying to the Caribbean, you can usually stay up a bit later on the first night and wake early, while flying east to Dubai or Asia means trying to sleep when your body thinks it's the afternoon.

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.text:
- **Warmest, with no time change at all:** Tenerife or Gran Canaria.
- **Properly hot, with a one-hour change:** Cape Verde.
- **Greener, for walking:** Madeira.
- **Culture with the sun:** Marrakech or Seville.
- **Shortest flight:** Málaga or the Algarve.

For more ideas by month, see [where to go in January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) and [where to go in February](/destinations/where-to-go-in-february). If you're travelling as a group and everyone has a different favourite, add them to a [somewhere.party](/) list and let the points decide.

faqs.question: Where is warm in winter with no time difference from the UK?
faqs.answer: The Canary Islands, such as Tenerife, Gran Canaria and Lanzarote, are on UK time all year and reach the low 20s in January. Madeira and mainland Portugal are on UK time too, though they're a little cooler.

faqs.question: What is the time difference in the Canary Islands?
faqs.answer: There isn't one. The Canary Islands are on the same time as the UK, and their clocks change on the same days in spring and autumn.

faqs.question: Is Cape Verde ahead of or behind the UK?
faqs.answer: Behind. Cape Verde is one hour behind the UK in winter and two hours behind during British Summer Time, because it doesn't change its clocks.

faqs.question: Is Morocco on the same time as the UK?
faqs.answer: Not usually. Morocco is normally one hour ahead of the UK in winter, but it switches its clocks back during Ramadan. Check the time difference for your travel dates.
